passages.text: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
passages.sermon:
This verse gives a warning.
\r\nIt speaks to every person.
\r\nDo not boast about tomorrow.
\r\nYou do not know what will happen tomorrow.
\r\nYou cannot see what each day will bring.
passages.original: אַֽל־ תִּ֭תְהַלֵּל בְּי֣וֹם מָחָ֑ר כִּ֤י לֹא־ תֵ֝דַ֗ע מַה־ יֵּ֥לֶד יֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Let another praise you, and not your own mouth— a stranger, and not your own lips.
passages.sermon:
A stranger should praise you.
You should not praise yourself.
Let someone else speak well of you.
Do not use your own lips to praise yourself.
passages.original: יְהַלֶּלְךָ֣ זָ֣ר וְלֹא־ פִ֑יךָ נָ֝כְרִ֗י וְאַל־ שְׂפָתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: A stone is heavy and sand is a burden, but aggravation from a fool outweighs them both.
passages.sermon:
A stone is heavy.
Sand is a burden.
Aggravation from a fool is worse than both.
Aggravation from a fool is harder to bear than a heavy stone or sand.
passages.original: כֹּֽבֶד־ אֶ֭בֶן וְנֵ֣טֶל הַח֑וֹל וְכַ֥עַס אֱ֝וִ֗יל כָּבֵ֥ד מִשְּׁנֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Wrath is cruel and anger is like a flood, but who can withstand jealousy?
passages.sermon: Wrath is cruel.\r\nAnger is like a flood.\r\nNo one can withstand jealousy.
passages.original: אַכְזְרִיּ֣וּת חֵ֭מָה וְשֶׁ֣טֶף אָ֑ף וּמִ֥י יַ֝עֲמֹד לִפְנֵ֥י קִנְאָֽה׃

passages.text: Better an open rebuke than love that is concealed.
passages.sermon: An open rebuke is better than hidden love.\r\nA clear correction is good.\r\nConcealed love is not as good as open correction.
passages.original: ט֭וֹבָה תּוֹכַ֣חַת מְגֻלָּ֑ה מֵֽאַהֲבָ֥ה מְסֻתָּֽרֶת׃

passages.text: The wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
passages.sermon:
A friend may wound you.
These wounds are faithful.
An enemy may kiss you.
These kisses are deceitful.
passages.original: נֶ֭אֱמָנִים פִּצְעֵ֣י אוֹהֵ֑ב וְ֝נַעְתָּר֗וֹת נְשִׁיק֥וֹת שׂוֹנֵֽא׃

passages.text: The soul that is full loathes honey, but to a hungry soul, any bitter thing is sweet.
passages.sermon:
A person who is satisfied does not want even honey.
A satisfied person turns away from sweet things.
A hungry person desires anything.
To a hungry person, even bitter food tastes sweet.
passages.original: נֶ֣פֶשׁ שְׂ֭בֵעָה תָּב֣וּס נֹ֑פֶת וְנֶ֥פֶשׁ רְ֝עֵבָ֗ה כָּל־ מַ֥ר מָתֽוֹק׃

passages.text: Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who wanders from his home.
passages.sermon:
A bird sometimes leaves its nest.
The bird moves away from its safe place.
A man can also leave his home.
The man wanders from the place where he belongs.
A man who leaves his home is like a bird that strays from its nest.
passages.original: כְּ֭צִפּוֹר נוֹדֶ֣דֶת מִן־ קִנָּ֑הּ כֵּֽן־ אִ֝֗ישׁ נוֹדֵ֥ד מִמְּקוֹמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Oil and incense bring joy to the heart, and the sweetness of a friend is counsel to the soul.
passages.sermon:
Oil brings joy to the heart.
Incense brings joy to the heart.
A friend gives sweet counsel.
Sweet counsel from a friend refreshes the soul.
passages.original: שֶׁ֣מֶן וּ֭קְטֹרֶת יְשַׂמַּֽח־ לֵ֑ב וּמֶ֥תֶק רֵ֝עֵ֗הוּ מֵֽעֲצַת־ נָֽפֶשׁ׃

passages.text: Do not forsake your friend or your father’s friend, and do not go to your brother’s house in the day of your calamity; better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.
passages.sermon:
A friend is someone who stands by you.
A father’s friend is also important.
Do not abandon your friend.
Do not abandon your father’s friend.
When trouble comes, do not go to your brother’s house.
A neighbor who is near can help you quickly.
A neighbor who is close is better than a brother who is far away.
passages.original: רֵֽעֲךָ֨ וְרֵעֶה אָבִ֡יךָ אַֽל־ תַּעֲזֹ֗ב וּבֵ֥ית אָחִ֗יךָ אַל־ תָּ֭בוֹא בְּי֣וֹם אֵידֶ֑ךָ ט֥וֹב שָׁכֵ֥ן קָ֝ר֗וֹב מֵאָ֥ח רָחֽוֹק׃

passages.text: Be wise, my son, and bring joy to my heart, so that I can answer him who taunts me.
passages.sermon:
A father speaks to his son.
He asks his son to be wise.
He says, “Be wise, my son.”
He says, “Bring joy to my heart.”
He wants to answer those who taunt him.
He says, “If you are wise, I can answer those who insult me.”
passages.original: חֲכַ֣ם בְּ֭נִי וְשַׂמַּ֣ח לִבִּ֑י וְאָשִׁ֖יבָה חֹרְפִ֣י דָבָֽר׃

passages.text: The prudent see danger and take cover; but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
passages.sermon:
A prudent person sees danger.
He takes cover.
A simple person keeps going.
He pays the penalty.
passages.original: עָר֤וּם רָאָ֣ה רָעָ֣ה נִסְתָּ֑ר פְּ֝תָאיִ֗ם עָבְר֥וּ נֶעֱנָֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: Take the garment of him who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.
passages.sermon:
A person may promise to pay a debt for a stranger.
This person puts himself at risk for someone he does not know.
Take his garment as security.
If he promises to pay for a foreigner, demand collateral from him.
This protects you from loss.
passages.original: קַח־ בִּ֭גְדוֹ כִּי־ עָ֣רַב זָ֑ר וּבְעַ֖ד נָכְרִיָּ֣ה חַבְלֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: If one blesses his neighbor with a loud voice early in the morning, it will be counted to him as a curse.
passages.sermon:
A person blesses his neighbor.
He uses a loud voice.
He does this early in the morning.
People count this blessing as a curse.
passages.original: מְבָ֘רֵ֤ךְ רֵעֵ֨הוּ׀ בְּק֣וֹל גָּ֭דוֹל בַּבֹּ֣קֶר הַשְׁכֵּ֑ים קְ֝לָלָ֗ה תֵּחָ֥שֶׁב לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: A constant dripping on a rainy day and a contentious woman are alike— restraining her is like holding back the wind or grasping oil with one’s right hand.
passages.sermon:
A constant dripping happens on a rainy day.
A contentious woman causes trouble.
A constant dripping and a contentious woman are alike.
You cannot restrain a contentious woman easily.
Trying to restrain her is like holding back the wind.
Trying to restrain her is like grasping oil with your right hand.
passages.original: דֶּ֣לֶף ט֭וֹרֵד בְּי֣וֹם סַגְרִ֑יר וְאֵ֥שֶׁת מְדוֹנִים נִשְׁתָּוָֽה׃ צֹפְנֶ֥יהָ צָֽפַן־ ר֑וּחַ וְשֶׁ֖מֶן יְמִינ֣וֹ יִקְרָֽא׃

passages.text: As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.
passages.sermon:
Iron can sharpen iron.
One man can sharpen another man.
Each person can help his friend become better.
People improve each other, just as iron improves iron.
passages.original: בַּרְזֶ֣ל בְּבַרְזֶ֣ל יָ֑חַד וְ֝אִ֗ישׁ יַ֣חַד פְּנֵֽי־ רֵעֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who looks after his master will be honored.
passages.sermon: A person who cares for a fig tree will eat its fruit.\r\nA person who serves his master will receive honor.
passages.original: נֹצֵ֣ר תְּ֭אֵנָה יֹאכַ֣ל פִּרְיָ֑הּ וְשֹׁמֵ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣יו יְכֻבָּֽד׃

passages.text: As water reflects the face, so the heart reflects the true man.
passages.sermon:
Water shows a reflection.
A person sees their own face in water.
The heart shows a person’s true self.
A person’s heart reveals who they really are to others.
passages.original: כַּ֭מַּיִם הַפָּנִ֣ים לַפָּנִ֑ים כֵּ֤ן לֵֽב־ הָ֝אָדָ֗ם לָאָדָֽם׃

passages.text: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
passages.sermon:
Sheol is the place of the dead.
Abaddon is the place of destruction.
Sheol is never satisfied.
Abaddon is never satisfied.
The eyes of man are never satisfied.
People always want more.
People are never fully content.
passages.original: שְׁא֣וֹל וַאֲבַדֹּה לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּ֑עְנָה וְעֵינֵ֥י הָ֝אָדָ֗ם לֹ֣א תִשְׂבַּֽעְנָה׃

passages.text: A crucible for silver and a furnace for gold, but a man is tested by the praise accorded him.
passages.sermon:
A crucible tests silver.
A furnace tests gold.
Praise tests a man.
People see a man's true character when others praise him.
passages.original: מַצְרֵ֣ף לַ֭כֶּסֶף וְכ֣וּר לַזָּהָ֑ב וְ֝אִ֗ישׁ לְפִ֣י מַהֲלָלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Though you grind a fool like grain with mortar and a pestle, yet his folly will not depart from him.
passages.sermon:
A fool is a person who acts without wisdom.
You can grind a fool in a mortar with a pestle.
You can crush him as if he were grain among the kernels.
His foolishness will not leave him.
His folly will remain with him.
passages.original: אִ֥ם תִּכְתּֽוֹשׁ־ אֶת־ הָאֱוִ֨יל׀ בַּֽמַּכְתֵּ֡שׁ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָ֭רִיפוֹת בַּֽעֱלִ֑י לֹא־ תָס֥וּר מֵ֝עָלָ֗יו אִוַּלְתּֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: Be sure to know the state of your flocks, and pay close attention to your herds; for riches are not forever, nor does a crown endure to every generation.
passages.sermon:
A wise person pays close attention to his animals.
He knows the condition of his flocks.
He carefully watches over his herds.
Riches do not last forever.
A crown does not remain for every generation.
passages.original: יָדֹ֣עַ תֵּ֭דַע פְּנֵ֣י צֹאנֶ֑ךָ שִׁ֥ית לִ֝בְּךָ֗ לַעֲדָרִֽים׃ כִּ֤י לֹ֣א לְעוֹלָ֣ם חֹ֑סֶן וְאִם־ נֵ֝֗זֶר לְד֣וֹר דּוֹר׃

passages.text: When hay is removed and new growth appears and the grain from the hills is gathered, the lambs will provide you with clothing, and the goats with the price of a field.
passages.sermon:
Hay is cut and taken away.
New grass grows and becomes visible.
People gather the plants from the hills.
Lambs give you wool for clothing.
Goats can be sold to buy a field.
passages.original: גָּלָ֣ה חָ֭צִיר וְנִרְאָה־ דֶ֑שֶׁא וְ֝נֶאֶסְפ֗וּ עִשְּׂב֥וֹת הָרִֽים׃ כְּבָשִׂ֥ים לִלְבוּשֶׁ֑ךָ וּמְחִ֥יר שָׂ֝דֶ֗ה עַתּוּדִֽים׃

passages.text: You will have plenty of goats’ milk to feed you— food for your household and nourishment for your maidservants.
passages.sermon:
You will have plenty of goats’ milk.
This milk will feed you.
This milk will provide food for your household.
This milk will give nourishment to your maidservants.
passages.original: וְדֵ֤י׀ חֲלֵ֬ב עִזִּ֗ים לְֽ֭לַחְמְךָ לְלֶ֣חֶם בֵּיתֶ֑ךָ וְ֝חַיִּ֗ים לְנַעֲרוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
